label: Copy-phase update gate: near end of short sequences, or when echoing o/a/y/r/d/p/k
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never on original-token steps or at <DEL>, and only when the input is a repeat of an earlier token (in_first == 0), which follows from the copy phase. Within the copy phase it fires on about 12% of steps. Two factors raise the firing rate. (1) Position: the last two outputs (to_go <= 1) hold 75% of the mass, and the effect is strongest for short sequences (L = 3 rate 0.33, L = 4 rate 0.11). The strongest activations are L = 3 sequences at the second copy step, e.g. u o h <DEL> u [o]. (2) Input-token identity: o (rate 0.20), a, y, r, d, p and k fire 2-4x above baseline at any copy position. The predicate gets dev F1 of about 0.43 with mass recall 0.85, but precision is about 0.3: many steps that satisfy the predicate stay silent, and activation is spread across positions and tokens without a sharp rule. Output token, previous token and correctness have little effect.
